narrative: This is an exceptionally well-architected orchestration skill with production-grade resume behavior, rigorous adversarial review isolation, and smart use of deterministic scripts. The primary opportunity is completing the automation story: three interaction points block headless execution, and the orchestrator's prompt layer carries ~1,000 tokens of template boilerplate that scripts could eliminate. Path reference issues (bare _bmad without {project-root}) need a quick fix.

broken.title: Bare _bmad reference without {project-root} prefix (contract anchor)
broken.detail: The customization preamble instruction references `_bmad/custom/<skill>.toml` without the `{project-root}` prefix. In a subagent context where the working directory may differ, this resolves to the wrong location.

broken.title: Bare _bmad reference without {project-root} prefix (config resolution)
broken.detail: The review model resolution references `_bmad/config.user.yaml` without the `{project-root}` prefix, creating the same working-directory resolution risk.

broken.title: uv not found — Python linting unavailable
broken.detail: The environment lacks uv, so ruff cannot lint the Python script. This is an environment setup issue, not a skill defect.

opportunities.name: Automation & Headless Readiness
opportunities.description: The skill is 80% of the way to headless-capable — --commit-policy, --skip-confirmations, and checkpoint-driven resume are already in place. But three interaction points block unattended execution: the mandatory Phase A review gate, decision-needed relays with no escalation policy, and orphaned worktree prompts with no default action. A CI pipeline invoking this skill will always stall.
opportunities.impact: Unlocks CI pipelines, chained-agent orchestration, and scheduled builds — the highest-value automation use cases for an epic-dev skill.
opportunities.action: Implement a --headless flag that auto-approves specs (with a log warning), fails fast on decision-needed relays, auto-cleans orphaned worktrees, and writes an epic-{N}-summary.json on completion/halt.

findings.title: Phase A review gate is un-overridable — blocks all CI/headless use
findings.detail: --skip-confirmations explicitly doesn't override the mandatory spec review gate. No flag exists to bypass it.

findings.title: No structured exit artifact — completion is prose only
findings.detail: The completion report is human-readable prose. CI pipelines need machine-readable JSON with story statuses, commit SHAs, and review verdicts.

findings.title: Decision-needed relays have no automation policy
findings.detail: When a subagent reports decision_needed, the orchestrator always halts for human input. No --on-decision=fail option for CI.

findings.title: No phase-entry flag for experts resuming partially-complete epics
findings.detail: Even when all stories are ready-for-dev, experts must walk through Step 0's full plan and approval. No --start-phase=B or auto-detection.

findings.title: Orphaned worktree prompt has no default action for automation
findings.detail: On resume, orphaned worktrees trigger an interactive prompt with no --clean-worktrees or --resume-worktrees default.

findings.title: Three-Mode Architecture incomplete — headless mode missing
findings.detail: Two modes exist (interactive + reduced-ceremony via --skip-confirmations). A true --headless mode with auto-approve, fail-fast, and structured output would complete the trifecta.

opportunities.name: Orchestrator Context Bloat from Templates & Read-Ahead
opportunities.description: The orchestrator reads four large subagent prompt templates (~600 tokens), reproduces them with variable substitution, and pre-reads story specs + diffs (~1,000–3,000 tokens per story) before delegating to review subagents. This bloats the parent's context window proportionally to layer width.
opportunities.impact: Eliminating template text and delegating reads would save ~920 tokens of static template cost plus 1,000–3,000 tokens per reviewed story in parent context, improving reliability for wide dependency layers.
opportunities.action: Build a render-prompt.py script that stores templates, accepts key-value args, and outputs fully rendered prompts. Refactor Phase B.2 to delegate diff extraction and spec reading to the review subagent.

findings.title: ~600 tokens of subagent prompt template text the LLM reads and reproduces
findings.detail: Four prompt templates (create-story, dev-story, code-review, fix-pass) are inline text that the LLM reads and reproduces with variable substitution.

findings.title: Customization preamble repeated verbatim 4× (~320 tokens)
findings.detail: The IMPORTANT — Team customizations block is copied identically into all four subagent templates.

findings.title: Parent reads diffs + specs before delegating to review subagents
findings.detail: For N stories in a layer, the parent accumulates N diffs + N specs in context — tokens it never uses beyond copy-pasting into prompts.

findings.title: Sequential per-story description before batch review launch
findings.detail: Steps 7a-7c describe per-story sequential flow, then step 8 says 'launch all simultaneously' — may cause LLM to process sequentially.

findings.title: Subagent return formats not JSON-enforced
findings.detail: Return fields specified in natural language rather than strict JSON schema, causing 50-200 tokens of conversational filler per response.

findings.title: Commit message templates could fold into prompt renderer
findings.detail: Three commit message templates with variable substitution are trivially deterministic.

findings.title: Config files loaded without explicit parallel instruction
findings.detail: Two config file reads not explicitly marked for parallel loading. Minor — small files, negligible impact.

opportunities.name: Unbounded Iteration Risks
opportunities.description: While the review fix cycle (B.3) is capped at 2 iterations, higher-level loops lack termination guards. The review-spawned story loop (B.7 → Phase A → Phase B) can theoretically cycle indefinitely. Circular dependencies are silently absorbed into orphan layers. Unknown-status stories are silently skipped.
opportunities.impact: Adding bounds prevents runaway subagent costs, infinite git history growth, and silent data loss from skipped stories.
opportunities.action: Add max_review_spawn_iterations (default: 2) for the B.7 loop. Detect circular dependencies in epic-plan.py and surface warnings. Treat unknown-status stories as backlog or warn explicitly.

findings.title: Review-spawned story loop (B.7→A→B) has no termination bound
findings.detail: B.7 loops back to Phase A when code review spawns new stories. A pathological review generating fix stories could loop indefinitely.

findings.title: No explicit iteration bound on Phase A ↔ B.7 outer loop
findings.detail: B.3's 2-cycle limit is well-bounded, but the outer Phase A → B → B.7 → Phase A loop has no equivalent guard.

findings.title: Circular dependencies silently placed in orphan layer
findings.detail: build_dependency_layers places unreachable stories in a final orphan layer without distinguishing circular deps from independent stories.

findings.title: Unknown-status stories silently skipped
findings.detail: Stories in the epic file but missing from sprint-status get status 'unknown' and don't match any Phase A/B filter — silently excluded.

opportunities.name: Reference Self-Containment Gaps
opportunities.description: Phase-logic.md back-references SKILL.md for commit-policy semantics and uses bare _bmad paths. During long-running orchestration, context compaction could drop SKILL.md, leaving the orchestrator without critical definitions.
opportunities.impact: Eliminates compaction risk for commit-policy behavior, reduces maintenance burden for model list, removes dead reference.
opportunities.action: Add a 1-line commit-policy definition to the contract anchor in phase-logic.md. Add a maintenance note for the model slug list. Remove user_name from the resolve list or document its purpose.

findings.title: Commit-policy semantics defined only in SKILL.md, not phase-logic.md
findings.detail: The valid values for --commit-policy (auto|ask|skip) and their behaviors are only in SKILL.md. If compacted during Phase B, semantics are lost.

findings.title: Model slug list hardcoded with no canonical-source note
findings.detail: Four model slugs are hardcoded. If the platform's available models change, this list becomes stale with no pointer to where it's maintained.

findings.title: user_name resolved but never referenced in workflow logic
findings.detail: On Activation resolves user_name from config, but neither SKILL.md nor phase-logic.md ever uses it. Creates a dead-reference appearance.

findings.title: Skip-confirmations behavior not defined in contract anchor
findings.detail: The contract anchor lists --skip-confirmations as an arg to respect but doesn't define what it suppresses. The name is self-documenting, but a one-line definition improves compaction resilience.

opportunities.name: Merge Conflict Recovery Gap
opportunities.description: The skill handles every failure mode with clear resume instructions — except merge conflicts, the most common real-world failure in a worktree-based parallel workflow. When a merge in B.4 fails, the user is left in an undocumented state.
opportunities.impact: Prevents the most frustrating failure mode in the workflow by giving users clear recovery steps and making resume deterministic after conflicts.
opportunities.action: Define a merge-conflict story state (or document exact manual recovery: resolve conflict, complete merge, mark done, clean worktree, re-invoke). Add partial-merge rollback guidance for multi-story layers.

findings.title: No merge-conflict state in resume behavior table
findings.detail: After a merge conflict, the story is marked 'review' (passed) but the merge failed. The resume table doesn't define what happens next.

findings.title: No partial-merge rollback guidance for multi-story layers
findings.detail: If story 2 of 3 conflicts during merge in B.4, story 1 is already merged. No guidance on whether to revert or resolve forward.

findings.title: Worktree failure recovery unspecified
findings.detail: B.1 assumes worktree creation succeeds. If it fails (branch exists, locked .git/worktrees), no orchestrator-level guidance.

strengths.title: Adversarial review isolation is architecturally enforced
strengths.detail: Dev and review use different subagent types, different LLM models, and zero context leakage. The contract anchor restates this at the top of phase-logic.md where it survives context compaction. This is the gold standard for automated code review.

strengths.title: epic-plan.py is a model script integration
strengths.detail: Offloading DAG computation, topological sort, and status cross-referencing to a deterministic Python script saves hundreds of LLM tokens and eliminates non-determinism. The script-first, LLM-fallback gate is the pattern all skills should follow.

strengths.title: Resume behavior is production-grade
strengths.detail: Sprint-status.yaml as the sole checkpoint, with story states mapping directly to resume positions, is elegant and robust. Orphaned worktree detection on resume handles real-world interrupted sessions.

strengths.title: Progressive disclosure is exemplary
strengths.detail: SKILL.md at 44 lines / 715 tokens is remarkably lean for an orchestrator managing specs, parallel dev, adversarial review, and fix cycles. All detail lives in references/phase-logic.md — loaded once per activation.

strengths.title: Contract anchor designed for compaction survival
strengths.detail: The clearly marked constraint block at the top of phase-logic.md places non-negotiable rules where they resist context window pressure during long-running orchestrations.

strengths.title: Dependency-layer parallelism is carefully reasoned
strengths.detail: Phase A parallelizes markdown specs (no conflicts). Phase B parallelizes via git worktrees (separate working directories). Sequential merge maintains linear history. This reflects genuine understanding of when parallelism is safe.

strengths.title: Intent guard prevents expensive mistakes
strengths.detail: Catching a single-story reference (e.g., '13.2') before launching a multi-hour full-epic orchestration is a small but high-value interaction pattern.

strengths.title: Bounded review fix cycles with escalation
strengths.detail: The 2-cycle cap in B.3 acknowledges that persistent review disagreements are likely design questions, not code fixes. Escalating to the user prevents infinite loops while preserving review rigor.

strengths.title: Self-contained subagent templates
strengths.detail: Each template includes customization loading, story context, specific instructions, output format, and scope guards (e.g., 'DO NOT run code review'). Subagents execute autonomously without external references.

strengths.title: Fail-forward within a layer
strengths.detail: In-flight dev subagents complete even when one fails, avoiding wasted work. New layers don't start until the current layer resolves, preventing cascading failures.

structure.assessment: Structurally sound with clean file organization: SKILL.md (entry), references/phase-logic.md (execution logic), scripts/epic-plan.py (deterministic computation), and scripts/tests/test-epic-plan.py (tests). Frontmatter is well-formed. The pre-pass classified the skill as simple-utility due to the absence of numbered stage files, but the skill actually implements complex multi-phase orchestration via its reference file — a valid design choice.

findings.title: Pre-pass type classification mismatch
findings.detail: Pre-pass detected simple-utility because there are no numbered stage files at root. The skill is actually a complex orchestration workflow. Informational for pre-pass algorithm improvement.

craft.assessment: Strong overview quality at 23 lines establishing mission, domain framing, and role clarity. Excellent progressive disclosure — SKILL.md at 44 lines / 715 tokens is among the leanest orchestrator skills possible while phase-logic.md carries the full execution detail. The contract anchor at the top of phase-logic.md is a standout defensive design pattern.

findings.title: Customization preamble repetition is structural necessity, not waste
findings.detail: Each of the 4 templates runs in isolated subagent context, so the repeated preamble is required. Acknowledged as well-designed by the prompt-craft scanner.

cohesion.assessment: Highly cohesive orchestration skill. Stage flow is logical — every phase builds on prior outputs. Parallelism strategy is carefully reasoned. The adversarial review contract is the most rigorous design element. Minor gaps in execution plan staleness after Phase A gate and cross-platform skill resolution.

stage_flow.notes: Clean linear top-level flow (Step 0 → A → B → Completion) with well-structured B sub-phases. No dead-end stages. B.7 elegantly closes the review-spawned story cycle.

purpose_alignment.notes: Promises match behavior. Design principles (orchestrator-not-implementer, fresh subagents, different review model, halt-on-failure) are consistently honored throughout.

complexity.notes: Complexity matches the task's decision space. epic-plan.py is a smart complexity reducer. B.6 sequential fallback adds necessary duplication.

gap_redundancy.notes: Execution plan may be stale after Phase A gate. Cross-platform skill resolution is fragile. No concurrent-epic guard.

findings.title: Execution plan may be stale after Phase A review gate
findings.detail: User is invited to edit specs during the review gate, but the execution plan (dependency layers, story list) is not re-computed afterward.

findings.title: Cross-platform skill resolution fragility
findings.detail: Sub-skills in .claude/skills/ resolved by name only from .cursor/skills/. If discovery mechanism changes, subagent prompts silently fail.

findings.title: B.6 sequential fallback positioned after B.5 but is an alternative execution mode
findings.detail: Cosmetic positioning issue — B.6 is an alternative to B.1-B.5, not a stage that runs after B.5. Could confuse a weaker model.

findings.title: No concurrent-epic guard
findings.detail: Nothing prevents running bmad-epic-dev for two epics simultaneously. Sprint-status.yaml is a shared file — concurrent writes could corrupt it.

efficiency.assessment: Well-optimized with dependency-layer parallelism, deterministic Python pre-pass, worktree-based isolation, and strict orchestrator-not-implementer contract. The main concern — parent context bloat from pre-reading diffs and specs — is addressed in the Orchestrator Context Bloat opportunity theme.

experience.assessment: The skill serves a wide range of users with varying levels of friction. First-timers benefit from intent guards and execution plan displays but lack coaching at the review gate. Experts appreciate --commit-policy and --skip-confirmations but want phase-entry and parallelism controls. The biggest gap is automation support — three interaction points block headless execution.

journeys.summary: A developer new to BMad types 'implement epic 16' and encounters worktrees, model routing, and a review gate with no coaching on what to verify.
friction_points: Worktree concept unexplained — extra directories appear with no context
Review model auto-selection has no qualitative guidance
Phase A review gate lists files but doesn't coach what to check
bright_spots: Intent guard catches single-story misfire elegantly
Execution plan display educates on epic structure and parallelism
Resume behavior means mistakes aren't catastrophic

journeys.summary: A power user with pre-reviewed specs wants maximum throughput but must walk through Step 0 approval and an un-overridable review gate.
friction_points: No phase-entry flag to skip to Phase B
Phase A review gate is un-overridable even with --skip-confirmations
No parallelism cap (--max-parallel) for resource-constrained environments
Review cycle limit (2) is hard-coded, not configurable

journeys.summary: User types 'dev epic 13' but may have meant deploy, status check, or a different epic number entirely.
friction_points: Intent guard only catches story-vs-epic confusion, not dev-vs-deploy
No 'list available epics' helper when epic number is wrong
No guard against accidental second invocation while subagents are running
bright_spots: Epic 'done' status detected immediately — cheap exit
Intent guard for story references works well

journeys.summary: Valid but unusual setups — circular dependencies, non-standard epic locations, unexpected story statuses — encounter silent failures.
friction_points: Circular dependencies produce orphan layers silently
Unknown-status stories silently skipped
Multi-epic concurrent execution unguarded
bright_spots: DAG re-parse on resume handles partial completion
Story status cross-referencing is thorough for known states

journeys.summary: Git worktree failures, model outages, or disk issues create recovery cliffs.
friction_points: Worktree creation failure recovery unspecified
Merge conflict recovery is a documentation cliff
Model unavailability mid-epic has no retry or fallback
Python version mismatch possible with epic-plan.py
bright_spots: Orphaned worktree detection on resume is thoughtful

journeys.summary: CI pipeline runs the skill with --commit-policy=auto --skip-confirmations but stalls at the mandatory review gate.
friction_points: Phase A review gate blocks all headless execution
No structured exit artifact for CI consumption
No timeout mechanism for hung subagents
Commit message format is not configurable

autonomous.notes: Three targeted flags (--headless, --on-decision=fail, --clean-worktrees) plus a JSON exit summary would make the skill fully headless-capable. The state machine is already externalized in sprint-status.yaml; only interaction points need parameterization.

findings.title: Phase A review gate coaching would transform gate from ceremony to value
findings.detail: A few bullets on what to verify (testable acceptance criteria, correct dependencies, scope alignment) would help first-timers use the gate effectively.

scripts.assessment: The existing epic-plan.py covers the heaviest deterministic block and is well-tested. However, ~1,970 tokens of additional deterministic work remain in the prompt layer — prompt rendering, review model resolution, sprint-status verification, git command construction, and worktree detection. A phased script buildout would eliminate this tax.

findings.title: Sprint-status verification at 3+ checkpoints could be scripted
findings.detail: Re-reading sprint-status.yaml to verify state transitions at multiple checkpoints is deterministic. ~250 tokens savings.

findings.title: Git diff command construction with exclude patterns
findings.detail: Two diff command templates with static exclude patterns and variable substitution. ~150 tokens savings.

findings.title: Git merge + cleanup command sequence
findings.detail: Fixed 4-command sequence (checkout, merge, worktree remove, branch delete) with variable substitution. ~120 tokens savings.

findings.title: Resume state→action mapping is a pure lookup table
findings.detail: A 5-row state-to-action table that could be a required_action field in epic-plan.py output. ~100 tokens savings.

recommendations.action: Add --headless automation mode (auto-approve specs, fail-fast on decisions, structured JSON exit artifact, auto-clean worktrees)
Build render-prompt.py for subagent prompt rendering — eliminate ~920 tokens of template boilerplate and delegate spec/diff reading to review subagents
Add iteration bounds to all loops — max_review_spawn_iterations (default 2), circular dependency detection in epic-plan.py, unknown-status story warnings
Fix path references and self-containment gaps — add {project-root} prefix to 2 bare paths, add commit-policy definition to contract anchor, document model slug maintenance source
Define merge conflict recovery — document exact manual recovery procedure, consider merge-conflict state in sprint-status, add partial-merge rollback guidance
Extend epic-plan.py with --resolve-review-model, --check-worktrees, and per-story required_action fields
